Let <MATH_0001> be a monomorphism of algebraic stacks.
Assume there exists a field <MATH_0002> and a locally finitely presented, surjective,
flat morphism <MATH_0003>. Then either <MATH_0004>
is empty or <MATH_0005> is an equivalence.

We may assume that <MATH_0001> is nonempty. In this case the
fibre product <MATH_0002>
is nonempty, see
Lemma <REF_0001>.
Now <MATH_0003> is an algebraic space and the projection <MATH_0004>
is a monomorphism. Hence <MATH_0005>, see
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0002>.
We conclude that <MATH_0006> factors through
<MATH_0007>. Suppose the morphism <MATH_0008>
is given by the object <MATH_0009> over <MATH_0010>. We have just seen that
<MATH_0011> is isomorphic to an object <MATH_0012> of <MATH_0013> over
<MATH_0014>. Since <MATH_0015>
is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation we see that
every object of <MATH_0016> over any scheme is fppf locally isomorphic
to a pullback of <MATH_0017>, hence also to a pullback of <MATH_0018>. By descent of
objects for stacks in groupoids this implies that
<MATH_0019> is essentially surjective (as well as
fully faithful, see
Lemma <REF_0003>).
Hence we win.

Let <MATH_0001> be an algebraic stack. Assume <MATH_0002> satisfies
the equivalent conditions of
Lemma <REF_0001>.
Then there exists a unique strictly full subcategory
<MATH_0003> such that
<MATH_0004> is an algebraic stack which satisfies the equivalent
conditions of
Lemma <REF_0002>.
The inclusion morphism <MATH_0005> is a monomorphism
of algebraic stacks.
